name: mikmod
why: A portable tracker player for old module music formats, a piece of old-school sound culture worth hearing.

brief.what_it_is: MikMod is a module player and library for tracker music, the old format family where a song is a set of patterns plus sampled instruments. The homepage says it supports many formats, including MOD, S3M, IT, and XM. The mikmod executable is the player, and libmikmod is the separate library that does the loading and mixing. Input is a tracker module file; output is audio sent to whichever sound driver the build uses. The homepage also says it was originally an MS-DOS player and has been ported to Unix, Macintosh, BeOS, and Java.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a portable way to play the module music of the DOS-era tracker scene across platforms. The scout note calls it a piece of old-school sound culture worth hearing. The homepage gives no separate mission statement.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. The changelogs describe per-format loaders (for example IT, XM, S3M, STM, AMF, GDM, MED, UNI, 669, FAR) and depackers for compressed modules, plus pluggable output drivers (ALSA, PulseAudio, SDL, OpenAL, WASAPI, CoreAudio, WinMM, OSS, and others). The library also exposes a reader/writer interface, which the changelog says custom implementations must respect.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps beyond the brew formula. The changelogs mention a configure script, a CMake build (which can install docs and an autoconf macro), standalone makefiles for DOS (djgpp), Windows (MinGW, Open Watcom, and Visual Studio project files), OS/2, and AmigaOS, and an option to disable all audio output drivers. Driver choice is made at build time through configure or CMake options. The homepage also lists a Ports and other versions page and a Where to get music page, which the fetched text did not reach.
brief.standout: It is a library first: libmikmod is the engine that many other players use, and the player is a thin front end on top of it. Its loader coverage of obscure tracker formats from DOS, Amiga, and Unreal-era games is unusually broad. Recent releases in 2026 were fixing crafted-file out-of-bounds writes and integer overflows, which suggests active fuzz-driven hardening of old parsers.
brief.status: Maintained, by the homepage's own news. The newest items are dated October 10 2026 (libmikmod 3.3.15 and 3.1.25). The player v3.2.10 and libmikmod 3.3.14 came out September 11 2026. The homepage also says the project stalled for a while and that maintainership passed to Shlomi Fish and then, in September 2013, to Ozkan. The brew formula's date and version were not checked.
brief.caveats: The homepage text was truncated before the Features, Screenshots, License, Files, Documentation, and Where to get music sections, so license and feature details are unverified. The documentation.html and features.html guesses returned 404, so I could not read the docs. Several drivers (PSP, Dreamcast, N64, Vita, gp32) are marked untested or were added without much testing. The homepage also says the Graoumf gt2 loader is non-functional and disabled. The SIMD option is disabled by default because it was marked unstable.
